changelog:
Films can be paused, sought and resumed, playback carries on when you leave the app, and the guide tells you what it is doing.

WHAT CHANGED

- Leaving the app while something plays shrinks it to a small window. Swipe the window away and the sound keeps playing, with controls in the notification to stop it.
- Films have a seek bar, skip back and forward, playback speed, a sleep timer, and a choice of audio and subtitle tracks.
- A film you stopped part way starts again where you left it, and posters show what you have watched and how far you got.
- Channel up and down step through the list you came from, and the zoom button says which zoom it is on.
- Refreshing the guide shows how far it has got and can be cancelled. Each source shows how many of its channels found a guide, after every refresh, including the ones the app runs on its own.
- Guide ids now match whatever their capitals, so some channels gain a guide. Channels that only had one through loose name guessing may lose it: that guessing put the wrong programmes on the wrong channels.
- New guide settings: how many days back and ahead, whether and how often it refreshes on its own, roughly what time, and a 12-hour clock.
- Guide times say "moments ago" rather than "0 minutes ago", and the guide shows how far ahead its listings reach.
- You can enter your own key for the film and series information service in Settings.
- Diagnostic mode in Settings keeps a log with your provider's details removed, ready to share when something goes wrong.

WHAT STAYS THE SAME

- Your sources, favourites, settings and pairing with your television.

NOT YET

- The guide's storage still grows a little with every refresh; the fix needs testing on a phone first.
- The Continue Watching row on the home screen is waiting on the same kind of testing.
